findings.explanation: high confidence. In Case 2.1, the author assumes that when only vertex a of the triangle T = {a, b, c} is at level 1, b and c at level 2 are discovered such that scanning the adjacency list of b will detect triangle {a, b, c}. However, b and c can be discovered through other vertices on level 1 (e.g., if s is also connected to x and y at level 1, with edges (x, b) and (y, c)). In this case, neither b nor c has a as its BFS parent. When edge (b, c) between level 2 vertices is encountered, it does not reveal the triangle {a, b, c} in O(1) time without verifying all common neighbors, causing the detection step to fail. Witness: A graph G where s is connected to a, x, y at level 1; x is connected to b, y is connected to c; and T = {a, b, c} is a triangle. Here only a in T is at level 1, but BFS discovers b via x and c via y, so neither b nor c has parent a.

evidence.text: Case 2.1: Exactly one vertex, namely a, appears on level 1.
